name: EMA Guideline on clinical evaluation of vaccines
description: Sets EU requirements for immunogenicity, efficacy and safety evidence for preventive vaccines, including use of immune markers as endpoints, dose and schedule selection, and evaluation of changes to licensed vaccines.
best_for: Justifying immunobridging and schedule selection for preventive vaccines
notes: Adopted and in force. EMEA/CHMP/VWP/164653/05 Rev. 1, effective August 2023.

name: EMA Guideline on immunogenicity assessment of therapeutic proteins
description: Sets EU expectations for anti-drug antibody assay strategy and risk factors, and how ADA incidence and neutralising capacity relate to changes in exposure, efficacy and safety.
best_for: Specifying ADA sampling and interpretation for EU submissions
notes: Adopted and in force. EMEA/CHMP/BMWP/14327/2006 Rev 1, effective December 2017.

name: EMA Guideline on PK evaluation in patients with decreased renal function
description: When and how to evaluate renal impairment in the EU, including renal function metrics, study designs, use of population PK, and the resulting SmPC dose recommendations.
best_for: P-10 and S2: EU renal impairment requirements
notes: Adopted. EMA/CHMP/725881/2015, effective July 2016, superseding CHMP/EWP/225/02.

name: EMA Guideline on PK evaluation in patients with impaired hepatic function
description: EU criteria for deciding whether a hepatic impairment study is needed, how to classify and recruit patients, and how findings translate into dosing advice in the SmPC.
best_for: P-11 and S2: EU hepatic impairment requirements
notes: Adopted. CPMP/EWP/2339/02, effective August 2005.

name: EMA Guideline on reporting the results of population pharmacokinetic analyses
description: What a population PK report submitted to EMA must contain - data handling, model-building rationale, diagnostics, validation and presentation - so an assessor can evaluate it.
best_for: S0-06 and S2: the EU counterpart to FDA's popPK guidance, and a usable report template
notes: Adopted. CHMP/EWP/185990/06, adopted June 2007, effective January 2008.

name: EMA Guideline on similar biological medicinal products: non-clinical and clinical issues
description: Sets EU non-clinical and clinical requirements for biosimilars: pharmacotoxicological assessment, comparative PK and PD study design, sensitivity of endpoints, efficacy, clinical safety and immunogenicity.
best_for: Aligning a biosimilar PK/PD similarity package with EU requirements
notes: Adopted and in force. EMEA/CHMP/BMWP/42832/2005 Rev1, effective July 2015, replacing the 2005 original.

name: EMA Guideline on the investigation of drug interactions
description: EU expectations for in vitro and clinical DDI evaluation, decision criteria for triggering studies, use of modelling, and how interaction findings must reach the SmPC.
best_for: The EU DDI reference alongside ICH M12
notes: Current effective version, marked under revision. CPMP/EWP/560/95/Rev.1 Corr.2, adopted 2012, last updated 2015.

name: EMA Guideline on the quality, non-clinical and clinical aspects of gene therapy medicinal products
description: Sets EU quality, non-clinical and clinical requirements for gene therapy products, including biodistribution and shedding characterisation, dose expression, and transgene-expression endpoints.
best_for: Defining biodistribution and transgene-expression endpoints for an EU gene therapy programme
notes: Adopted and in force. EMA/CAT/80183/2014, published July 2018, Revision 1 of the 2001 guidance.

name: EMA Guideline on the reporting of PBPK modelling and simulation
description: What a PBPK report must document, including platform and model qualification proportionate to the regulatory impact of the intended use.
best_for: S3 PBPK: the EU expectations on model qualification and reporting
notes: Adopted. EMA/CHMP/458101/2016, published December 2018, effective July 2019. The adopted title is 'reporting of PBPK' - 'qualification and reporting' was the draft title and should not be cited.

name: EMA opinions and letters of support on qualification of novel methodologies
description: The catalogue of CHMP qualification opinions and letters of support, with disease-specific entries for Alzheimer's biomarkers, Parkinson's DAT imaging, ADPKD kidney volume, Duchenne stride velocity and COPD fibrinogen.
best_for: The authoritative free register of which disease-specific methodologies European regulators have formally qualified
notes: All documents are free downloadable PDFs with no registration. What is qualified is the methodology; model code is generally not attached.

name: EMA Qualification opinion: in vitro hollow fibre system model of tuberculosis
description: CHMP opinion endorsing the hollow fibre system as a complementary tool informing anti-tuberculosis dose and regimen selection across phases I to III, covering time-above-MIC and AUC/MIC targets and Monte Carlo dose simulation.
best_for: Reading exactly what regulators accepted an in vitro PK/PD system for, and the evidentiary standard applied
notes: Adopted January 2015. Qualifies a method rather than a distributable model, but describes the metabolic states and simulation workflow in enough detail to reimplement.

name: FDA Assessing the Effects of Food on Drugs in INDs and NDAs
description: When and how to run food-effect studies for oral products, meal composition and design, and how the resulting exposure changes drive administration instructions in labelling.
best_for: P-06 absorption: the regulatory counterpart to the BDDCS food-effect literature
notes: Final, Level 2, May 2026, CDER. Supersedes portions of the earlier 2002 food-effect document.

name: FDA Bispecific Antibody Development Programs
description: Addresses regulatory, quality, nonclinical and clinical considerations for bispecific antibodies, including whether the parent monospecific components must be characterised separately and how dose selection is justified.
best_for: Framing dose-finding and comparator strategy for bispecific and multispecific constructs
notes: Final Level 1, May 2021, CBER and CDER. Principles may inform other multispecific protein products.

name: FDA Clinical Considerations for Therapeutic Cancer Vaccines
description: Covers phase 1-2 and phase 3 design for therapeutic cancer vaccines, including delayed effect on endpoints, dose and schedule selection, and immune-response measurement.
best_for: Endpoint and schedule selection where clinical benefit is delayed relative to immune activation
notes: Final, October 2011, CBER.

name: FDA Clinical Pharmacology Considerations for Antibody-Drug Conjugates
description: Specifies which ADC analytes to measure - conjugate, total antibody and unconjugated payload - and the expectations for dosing strategy, exposure-response, QTc, immunogenicity and drug-interaction assessment.
best_for: Designing multi-analyte PK sampling and exposure-response analyses for cytotoxic-payload ADCs
notes: Final Level 1, March 2024, CDER and CBER. States the principles may not apply to non-cytotoxic-payload ADCs.

name: FDA Clinical Pharmacology Considerations for Human Radiolabeled Mass Balance Studies
description: Whether and when to conduct a human ADME mass balance study, how to design it, and how to present recovery, metabolite profiling and routes-of-elimination results.
best_for: P-09 and P-10: how anyone knows a drug's actual elimination route
notes: Final, September 2024, CDER.

name: FDA Clinical Pharmacology Considerations for Oligonucleotide Therapeutics
description: Specifies four assessments for antisense and siRNA products: QTc prolongation, immunogenicity risk, the effect of hepatic and renal impairment on exposure, and drug-interaction potential.
best_for: Planning the clinical pharmacology package and organ-impairment covariate analysis for ASO and siRNA programmes
notes: Final, June 2024, CDER.

name: FDA Clinical Pharmacology Considerations for Peptide Drug Products
description: Addresses hepatic impairment, drug interaction, QTc and immunogenicity assessment for peptide products submitted under the NDA pathway, where neither small-molecule nor therapeutic-protein defaults apply.
best_for: Deciding which clinical pharmacology studies a peptide NDA requires
notes: Draft Level 2, December 2023, CDER. The gap it fills - peptides sit between two regulatory frameworks - is the reason it exists.

name: FDA Clinical Pharmacology Data to Support a Demonstration of Biosimilarity
description: Defines the exposure and response assessment supporting a 351(k) application: study population and design, PK and PD endpoint selection, sensitivity of PD markers, and similarity acceptance criteria.
best_for: Designing and analysing comparative PK/PD similarity studies
notes: Final, December 2016, CDER and CBER.

name: FDA Considerations for the Design of Early-Phase Clinical Trials of Cellular and Gene Therapy Products
description: Addresses starting dose justification, escalation scheme, staggering, subject selection and feasibility endpoints for first-in-human cellular and gene therapy trials.
best_for: Justifying a starting dose where conventional PK exposure metrics do not apply
notes: Final, June 2015, CBER.

name: FDA Considerations for the Development of CAR T Cell Products
description: Covers CMC, pharmacology and clinical study design for autologous and allogeneic CAR T cells, including analytical comparability after a manufacturing change and definition of dose by cell number.
best_for: Framing cellular kinetics, dose definition and comparability for engineered cell products
notes: Final, January 2024, CBER. Also applies to CAR NK and TCR-modified T cells.

name: FDA Considerations in Demonstrating Interchangeability With a Reference Product
description: Sets expectations for switching-study design and endpoints, including PK and immunogenicity endpoints across alternating exposure periods, to support an interchangeability determination.
best_for: Designing and powering switching studies with PK and ADA endpoints
notes: Final Level 1, May 2019. A June 2024 draft update revises its switching-study recommendations.

name: FDA Exposure-Response Relationships
description: How to design studies and analyse data to characterise exposure-response for efficacy and safety, and how E-R evidence can support dose selection and labelling.
best_for: S1 PK/PD and exposure-response; foundational reading for dose justification
notes: Final, May 2003, CDER and CBER. Still the current FDA E-R guidance.

name: FDA General Principles for the Development of Vaccines to Protect Against Global Infectious Diseases
description: Sets the regulatory and statutory framework for licensing vaccines against diseases endemic outside the United States, including evidence generation when trials are conducted in endemic regions.
best_for: Planning licensure evidence for vaccines against non-US-endemic pathogens
notes: Final, December 2011, CBER.

name: FDA Human Gene Therapy Products Incorporating Human Genome Editing
description: States the IND content expected for somatic genome-editing products: editing component design, on- and off-target activity characterisation, manufacturing and testing, nonclinical safety and trial design.
best_for: Structuring off-target activity evidence and first-in-human design for genome-editing products
notes: Final, January 2024, CBER.

name: FDA Immunogenicity Assessment for Therapeutic Protein Products
description: Sets a risk-based approach to evaluating and mitigating immune responses to therapeutic proteins, including the product, patient and treatment factors that alter clearance, exposure and response.
best_for: Building anti-drug antibody status into PK and exposure-response models for mAbs and Fc-fusion proteins
notes: Final, August 2014, CDER and CBER.

name: FDA Immunogenicity Testing of Therapeutic Protein Products: Developing and Validating Assays for Anti-Drug Antibody Detection
description: Specifies the tiered screening, confirmatory, titre and neutralising-antibody assay scheme and its validation parameters, including cut-point determination and drug tolerance.
best_for: Understanding what an ADA titre means, and its drug-tolerance limits, before using ADA as a model covariate
notes: Final, February 2019, CDER and CBER. Drug tolerance is the parameter most often ignored when ADA is treated as a binary covariate.

name: FDA In Vitro Drug Interaction Studies - CYP Enzyme- and Transporter-Mediated
description: Which in vitro CYP and transporter experiments to run, the cut-off criteria and basic static models that decide whether a clinical DDI study or a PBPK simulation is needed.
best_for: P-09 and P-03: the in vitro to clinical decision tree
notes: Final, January 2020, CDER.

name: FDA IND Submissions for Individualized Antisense Oligonucleotide Products: Clinical Recommendations
description: Addresses starting dose, escalation and monitoring for n-of-1 antisense products targeting variants unique to one or two participants, and when a broader development programme should be pursued instead.
best_for: Dose selection where the trial population is a single patient - the limiting case of individualised dosing
notes: Draft Level 1, December 2021, CDER. Draft status as stated on the page.

name: FDA Long Term Follow-up After Administration of Human Gene Therapy Products
description: Defines the product-attribute risk assessment - persistence, integration, latency, transgene expression - that determines whether long-term follow-up observations are needed and for how long.
best_for: Setting the duration and endpoints of delayed-adverse-event follow-up for vector-based therapies
notes: Final, January 2020, CBER.

name: FDA Model-Informed Drug Development Paired Meeting Program
description: The PDUFA programme letting sponsors bring a specific MIDD question to FDA in paired meetings; sets eligibility, submission content and the meeting sequence.
best_for: S0-00: how modelling questions actually reach FDA
notes: Programme page, not a guidance. Current as of July 2026, covering fiscal years 2023-2027. The page recommends sponsors use ICH M15 when preparing meeting requests.

name: FDA Nonclinical Evaluation of Late Radiation Toxicity of Therapeutic Radiopharmaceuticals
description: Describes nonclinical study design for irreversible late radiation effects in normal organs from agents delivering ionizing radiation, complementing general nonclinical safety expectations.
best_for: Relating absorbed dose in normal organs to late toxicity risk before clinical radioligand trials
notes: Final, November 2011, CDER.

name: FDA Oncology Therapeutic Radiopharmaceuticals: Dosage Optimization During Clinical Development
description: Addresses selection of administered activity, number of cycles and interval for therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals in oncology. Explicitly excludes dosimetry software and personalised-dosimetry dosing from its scope.
best_for: Structuring dose-optimisation trials for radioligand therapy under Project Optimus principles
notes: Draft, August 2025, Oncology Center of Excellence. That dosimetry is excluded from scope is itself the notable point.

name: FDA Optimizing the Dosage of Drugs for the Treatment of Oncologic Diseases
description: How to identify an optimised oncology dosage before a marketing application, including randomised comparison of multiple dosages and the PK/PD and exposure-response evidence expected.
best_for: The operative guidance implementing Project Optimus; dose-selection work in oncology
notes: Final, August 2024, Oncology Center of Excellence with CDER and CBER.

name: FDA Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Hepatic Function
description: When a hepatic impairment study is warranted, Child-Pugh-based design and analysis, and how the PK findings feed dosing and labelling.
best_for: P-11 and S2: hepatic covariate effects and dose adjustment
notes: Final, May 2003, CDER and CBER.

name: FDA Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Renal Function
description: When to study renal impairment, reduced versus full study designs, which renal function measure to use, and how results translate into dosing recommendations in labelling.
best_for: P-10 and S2: covariate analysis and dose adjustment
notes: Final, Level 1, March 2024 - this is now final and dated 2024, not the 2020 draft.

name: FDA Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Analyses - Format and Content
description: What a PBPK submission must contain: a prescribed six-section report structure covering model assumptions, parameters, verification and sensitivity analyses.
best_for: S3 PBPK: how to write up a PBPK analysis for a regulator
notes: Final, September 2018, CDER.

name: FDA Population Pharmacokinetics
description: When a population PK analysis is expected, how to build and evaluate the model, and what the analysis plan, report and data files must contain to support labelling and dose individualisation.
best_for: S2 population PK: model development, evaluation and the submission-ready report
notes: Final, Level 1 guidance, February 2022. CDER and CBER. Finalises the 2019 draft.

name: FDA Potency Assurance for Cellular and Gene Therapy Products
description: Describes a risk-based potency assurance strategy spanning process design, in-process controls and release assays so that each lot retains the capacity to produce the intended therapeutic effect.
best_for: Linking potency assay design and acceptance criteria to dose definition for cell and gene therapies
notes: Draft, December 2023, CBER. Not for implementation.

name: FDA Project Optimus
description: Oncology Center of Excellence initiative to replace MTD-driven oncology dosing with dose optimisation balancing efficacy, safety and tolerability before registration.
best_for: The policy context behind randomised dose-ranging in oncology
notes: An initiative page, not a guidance document. Page content current as of December 2024.

name: FDA Scientific Considerations in Demonstrating Biosimilarity: Updated Recommendations on Comparative Efficacy Studies
description: Sets when a comparative clinical study with efficacy endpoints can be omitted, placing the weight of evidence on analytical characterisation and comparative human PK, PD and immunogenicity data.
best_for: The clearest current statement of PK/PD evidence substituting for a clinical efficacy trial
notes: Draft, October 2025, CDER. The page does not state that it supersedes the April 2015 final guidance.

name: FDA Status of Biomarker Qualification Submissions
description: Gateway for tracking biomarker qualification submissions through letters of intent, qualification plans and full packages, and for locating qualified biomarkers with their disease context of use.
best_for: Checking whether a disease-specific biomarker has actually been qualified, and at what stage others sit
notes: Free but indirect: the page does not tabulate qualified biomarkers itself, it directs you to filter the DDT qualification project search database.

name: ICH E11(R1) Clinical Investigation of Medicinal Products in the Pediatric Population
description: Current regulatory perspective on paediatric trial design, age classification, extrapolation concepts and paediatric formulation, updating ICH E11 for modern practice.
best_for: P-12: the framing document for paediatric PK study design
notes: Final, April 2018. Complements rather than replaces the original ICH E11 of 2000.

name: ICH E11A Pediatric Extrapolation
description: A systematic approach to paediatric extrapolation: building the extrapolation concept, quantifying similarity in exposure and response, and designing the confirmatory evidence package.
best_for: P-12 and S3: modelling-driven paediatric dose selection
notes: Final, December 2024. Replaces the August 2022 draft.

name: ICH E14 and S7B QT/QTc Prolongation Questions and Answers
description: How integrated nonclinical and clinical evidence, including concentration-QTc modelling, can substitute for a dedicated thorough QT study and what the analysis must demonstrate.
best_for: P-16 safety: concentration-QTc modelling
notes: Final, August 2022. Revises Q12/Q13 of ICH E14 and adds questions to ICH S7B.

name: ICH E4 Dose-Response Information to Support Drug Registration
description: The foundational requirement that registration dossiers characterise dose-response, not just show one dose works; covers parallel, titration and crossover dose-response designs.
best_for: P-14 dose-response: the origin of the regulatory demand for dose-response evidence
notes: ICH Step 4, dated 10 March 1994. ICH publishes no per-guideline landing page for E4, so the database PDF is the canonical link.

name: ICH M10 Bioanalytical Method Validation and Study Sample Analysis
description: Harmonised validation requirements for chromatographic and ligand-binding assays, plus study sample analysis and reporting expectations that determine whether concentration data are usable.
best_for: S0-03: where the concentrations feeding a popPK model come from, and what LLOQ actually means
notes: Final, November 2022. Replaces the M10 draft of June 2019.

name: ICH M12 Drug Interaction Studies
description: The harmonised ICH framework for enzyme- and transporter-mediated DDI evaluation: in vitro triggers, clinical study design, model-based approaches and how results reach the label.
best_for: The current international DDI reference, replacing region-specific clinical DDI guidance
notes: Final, Level 1, August 2024. Replaces the 2022 draft. In practice this now stands in for FDA's withdrawn 2020 Clinical Drug Interaction Studies guidance, whose page no longer resolves.

name: ICH M15 General Principles for Model-Informed Drug Development
description: The first harmonised MIDD framework: defining context of use, model credibility assessment proportional to regulatory impact, and the documentation expected for any model in a submission.
best_for: The umbrella document above popPK, PBPK, exposure-response and QSP guidance - read this first
notes: Final, Level 1, June 2026. The newest document in the set; confirm currency before citing.

name: ICH S12 Nonclinical Biodistribution Considerations for Gene Therapy Products
description: Harmonises nonclinical biodistribution study design for gene therapy products: analyte and matrix selection, sampling time points, assay validation, and interpretation of vector persistence and expression.
best_for: Designing and interpreting the vector biodistribution studies that inform clinical dose and follow-up
notes: Step 4 final, 14 March 2023. This is the closest thing gene therapy has to a pharmacokinetics guideline.

name: PMDA Biosimilars guidelines and notifications
description: Collection hosting the Japanese Guideline for Ensuring Quality, Safety and Efficacy of Biosimilars and its Q and A documents, defining comparability expectations including comparative PK and immunogenicity data.
best_for: Checking Japanese comparability and PK-similarity requirements for a biosimilar filing
notes: Landing page; documents are not labelled draft or final. Guideline dated February 2020, with Q and A updates through 2026.

name: PMDA Guideline for Exposure-Response Analysis of Drugs
description: Japan's framework for planning, conducting and reporting exposure-response analyses of efficacy and safety, and how E-R evidence supports dose selection.
best_for: S1: the Japanese counterpart to FDA's 2003 exposure-response guidance
notes: MHLW notification dated 8 June 2020. English text is a provisional translation; the Japanese version prevails.

name: PMDA Guideline on Population Pharmacokinetic and Pharmacodynamic Analysis
description: Japan's expectations for population PK/PD analysis: study planning, data handling, model development and validation, and the content of the analysis plan and report.
best_for: S2: the Japanese counterpart to FDA and EMA popPK guidance
notes: MHLW notification PSEHB/PED No. 0515-1, 15 May 2019. The English text is an explicitly provisional translation; the Japanese version is official.

name: PMDA Guidelines for Analysis Reports Involving PBPK Models
description: What a PBPK analysis report submitted in Japan must contain - model structure, parameter sources, verification against observed data, and the intended regulatory application.
best_for: S3: completes the FDA/EMA/PMDA trio of PBPK reporting standards
notes: MHLW notification PSEHB/PED No. 1221-1, 21 December 2020. English provided for reference only; the Japanese original prevails.

name: PMDA Regenerative Medical Products guidelines and notifications
description: Collection of the Japanese regulatory framework for cell and gene therapy: quality and safety guidelines by cell source, gene therapy and genome-editing notifications, and the conditional approval pathway.
best_for: Locating Japanese requirements for cell and gene therapy, including the conditional time-limited approval route
notes: Landing page; documents are not labelled draft or final. Dates range from 2008 to 2025.

name: ncappc
description: Traditional non-compartmental analysis plus simulation-based posterior predictive checks that diagnose a population PK model using NCA metrics.
best_for: Checking whether a popPK model reproduces the NCA metrics of the observed data
notes: The NCA-based PPC diagnostic is the unusual part. Low GitHub activity - for plain NCA, PKNCA is the busier project.

name: Phoenix WinNonlin
description: Desktop workflow tool for non-compartmental analysis, compartmental PK/PD and toxicokinetics, from data preparation to report output.
best_for: NCA and bioequivalence work of the kind submitted to regulators
notes: Pricing not published. Certara offers free licences for academic users teaching a course - tied to teaching, not general student use.

name: PKNCA
description: Non-compartmental analysis of PK data covering dense and sparse sampling, unit handling, imputation, CDISC-formatted output and bioequivalence assessment.
best_for: Free, scriptable NCA as an alternative to Phoenix WinNonlin
notes: AGPL-3 is the strongest copyleft here - relevant if you plan to embed it in a hosted service.

name: AMICI
description: Python/C++ interface to SUNDIALS CVODES and IDAS that imports SBML or PySB models, generates optimised C++, and computes forward, steady-state and adjoint sensitivities.
best_for: Gradient-based parameter estimation of large QSP models where finite-difference gradients are too slow
notes: Not a GUI - you supply the model and it compiles it; needs a working C++ toolchain. Pairs with PEtab.

name: Catalyst.jl
description: Symbolic Julia package for chemical reaction networks: one specification generates ODE, SDE, stochastic jump, steady-state and hybrid simulations, with symbolic Jacobians.
best_for: Performance-critical or stochastic systems-pharmacology models, and the SciML sensitivity ecosystem
notes: Julia-only, and the ecosystem moves fast with breaking releases. Smaller pharmacometrics user base than R or Python equivalents.

name: libRoadRunner
description: Simulation engine compiling SBML models to machine code, running time courses, steady state, stochastic simulation, sensitivity analysis and metabolic control analysis via C++, C or Python.
best_for: The fast SBML solver underneath a larger workflow when repeated simulation speed matters
notes: A library, not an application - most learners meet it indirectly through Tellurium.

name: Tellurium
description: Python environment for systems-biology modelling bundling the libRoadRunner engine and the Antimony human-readable model language, with SBML, SED-ML and COMBINE support.
best_for: Writing a reaction network in readable text, simulating it fast, and exporting reproducible SBML/SED-ML
notes: Tellurium itself is Apache-2.0 but it is a bundle - constituent packages carry various licences.

name: GastroPlus
description: PBPK/PBBM platform focused on oral absorption: predicting dissolution and absorption from formulation and structure, preclinical-to-human translation, DDI and bioequivalence.
best_for: Oral absorption and formulation/biopharmaceutics questions, and virtual bioequivalence
notes: Commercial, closed-source, time-limited evaluation only. Its absorption module is the distinguishing feature - not interchangeable with Simcyp or PK-Sim on DDI or population physiology.

name: Open Systems Pharmacology Suite (PK-Sim and MoBi)
description: PK-Sim for whole-body PBPK models with built-in human and lab-animal physiology, and MoBi for custom PBPK/PD and QSP models, exchanged via the PKML format.
best_for: Learning whole-body PBPK end to end without a licence fee
notes: Genuinely open source and free for everyone including commercial use - unusual for PBPK, where the alternatives are expensive. Windows-centric GUI; scripting is via the separate ospsuite R package. Video tutorials and docs are open without registration.

name: ospsuite (OSPSuite-R)
description: R package to load, modify and run simulations created in PK-Sim and MoBi: change parameters, run population simulations, PK analysis, sensitivity analysis, import and plot data.
best_for: Scripting reproducible PBPK workflows on top of a model built in the PK-Sim GUI
notes: Not a standalone simulator - the GUI suite still has to be installed. Distributed from GitHub, not CRAN.

name: Simcyp PBPK Simulator
description: Population PBPK platform for first-in-human dose prediction, drug-drug interaction screening, paediatric and special-population modelling, and formulation assessment.
best_for: Understanding what regulatory-grade population PBPK looks like in industry
notes: Closed commercial software with no free tier. Regulatory acceptance is real - EMA qualification and use in many approved drugs - but access is not. An academic scheme exists for institutions already holding a paid licence.

name: DILIsym, RENAsym, NAFLDsym and related QSP libraries
description: Pre-built disease-area QSP model libraries: drug-induced liver injury, acute kidney injury, steatotic liver disease, interstitial lung disease and pulmonary fibrosis.
best_for: Seeing what an industrially maintained, disease-specific QSP platform contains
notes: Licensed model libraries, not a modelling language: you cannot rebuild them, and the model structure is not published in full.

name: FDA CiPA in silico proarrhythmia model code
description: Code for uncertainty quantification of the CiPA cardiac model: hERG gating with drug-binding kinetics, concentration-response for six ionic currents, and propagation of that uncertainty into action-potential simulations.
best_for: Running the regulatory cardiac-safety proarrhythmia model and seeing how parameter uncertainty reaches an action-potential endpoint
notes: Public FDA repository, GPL-3, R with C solvers. Weak maintenance signal - three commits, no releases, and an explicit FDA disclaimer for third-party use. Pairs with P-16.

name: IQR Tools
description: R toolbox spanning systems biology, QSP, PBPK, PK/PD and clinical trial simulation, providing a common model definition that drives NONMEM, Monolix and nlmixr for estimation.
best_for: Running one model definition across several estimation engines
notes: Free for academia, non-profits and government; others request a quote. Free to use is not open source, and the NONMEM/Monolix back-ends are separately licensed.

name: OpenMalaria
description: Stochastic simulator of malaria epidemiology and of the population-level impact of interventions, with scenarios defined through an XML schema.
best_for: Simulating population-level malaria intervention impact rather than individual exposure-response
notes: Strong maintenance signal - 2,905 commits and three institutional maintainers. Epidemiological rather than pharmacometric: the repository page does not confirm within-host parasite or drug PK components.

name: PhysiPKPD
description: Drug-treatment module for the PhysiCell agent-based framework, implementing constant, one- and two-compartment and SBML-defined PK models and AUC- or damage-mediated PD, coupled through substrate diffusion and cellular uptake.
best_for: Linking a conventional compartmental PK model to a spatial agent-based tumour simulation
notes: MIT licensed, 421 commits with sample projects and test infrastructure - a good maintenance signal for an academic model.

name: QSPIO-TNBC
maintainer: Popel Systems Biology Laboratory, Johns Hopkins University
description: Modular immuno-oncology QSP platform for triple-negative breast cancer and NSCLC covering antigen presentation, T cell dynamics and the tumour microenvironment, with modules for checkpoint inhibitors, T cell engagers and ADCs.
best_for: Inspecting virtual-patient generation and checkpoint-inhibitor mechanism structure in a complete, runnable IO model
notes: MIT licensed but requires MATLAB R2020b with the commercial SimBiology, Symbolic Math and Statistics toolboxes - free to copy, not free to run. Supersedes the older popellab/qspio.

name: QSPy
description: PySB-based Python framework for modular construction and simulation of rule-based QSP models of drug interaction with biological systems.
best_for: Adding PK/PD and dosing conventions on top of PySB rather than re-implementing them per project
notes: Explicitly early-stage: a Work in Progress badge and version 0.1.0, no stable release. Do not build coursework on it expecting API stability.

name: SimBiology
description: MATLAB toolbox to build, simulate and analyse QSP, PBPK and PK/PD models: parameter estimation, sensitivity analysis, Monte Carlo simulation and NCA.
best_for: QSP model building in teams already standardised on MATLAB, especially virtual-population work
notes: Requires a paid MATLAB licence on top of the toolbox licence - the diagram interface can look free-standing but is not.

name: Ubiquity PKPD Tools
description: Modelling system for PK, PD and QSP models: a system-file model description translated into R and MATLAB workflows, with parameter sets, NCA, pooled estimation, trial simulation and reporting.
best_for: A free, scriptable QSP/PKPD workflow with a built-in Shiny app for exploring a model
notes: Free and BSD-licensed, but a small single-maintainer project. The MATLAB workflow needs MATLAB; the R workflow does not.

name: lme4
description: Fits linear, generalized linear and nonlinear mixed-effects models with nested and crossed random effects, likelihood profiling and parametric bootstrap.
best_for: Learning what random effects actually are, on ordinary hierarchical data, before meeting PK-specific NLME software
notes: Not pharmacometrics software: no dosing records, no ODE compartments. Useful as statistical background, misleading if treated as a popPK tool.

name: pmxTools
description: Closed-form concentration calculations for 1-, 2- and 3-compartment models with various absorption, infusion, lag-time and steady-state cases, plus parsing of NONMEM and PsN output.
best_for: Quick closed-form PK calculations and pulling NONMEM results into R
notes: The closed-form functions are useful with no NONMEM installed; the output-parsing half assumes NONMEM or PsN runs exist.

name: ggPMX
maintainer: ggPMX development team; copyright Novartis Pharma AG
description: ggplot2 toolbox producing publication-quality diagnostic plots and tables - residuals, EBE plots, distributions, VPCs - from Monolix, NONMEM and nlmixr fits.
best_for: One consistent diagnostic plot set across different estimation engines
notes: Built at Novartis to standardise diagnostics following ISoP guidance. Monolix support needs the lixoftConnectors package.

name: tidyvpc
description: Computes VPC percentiles and prediction intervals with a tidyverse-style piped interface. Supports stratification, censoring, prediction correction, binning and binless methods.
best_for: VPCs needing binless methods, censoring or prediction correction handled properly
notes: Free and MIT-licensed even though Certara maintains it - no Certara licence needed.

name: vpc
description: R package for creating visual predictive checks, the standard simulation-based diagnostic plot in pharmacometrics.
best_for: Producing a VPC regardless of which engine produced the simulations
notes: Engine-agnostic: you supply the simulation output. Installed from GitHub. tidyvpc is a more actively developed alternative.

name: xpose
maintainer: Benjamin Guiastrennec, Andrew Hooker, Sebastian Ueckert, Mats Karlsson
description: ggplot2-based diagnostics for nonlinear mixed-effects population models. Imports NONMEM output and produces goodness-of-fit plots, individual profiles and VPCs.
best_for: Modern, customisable NONMEM diagnostic plots you can restyle with ggplot2
notes: The ggplot2 rewrite of xpose4 - pick this for new work. Reads NONMEM output, so presumes a NONMEM licence somewhere.

name: Xpose 4
maintainer: Andrew Hooker, Mats Karlsson, Niclas Jonsson
description: Model-building aid for nonlinear mixed-effects population analysis with NONMEM: data exploration, visualisation, model diagnostics, covariate identification and model comparison.
best_for: Classic NONMEM diagnostics, and reproducing plots from older papers and courses
notes: The older lattice-based generation. Much teaching material still assumes xpose4, which is why both exist.

name: MIRDcalc
maintainer: University of Florida and Memorial Sloan Kettering
description: Organ-level internal dosimetry calculator implementing the MIRD schema, with 333 radionuclides, 12 ICRP reference phantoms, 81 source and 43 target regions, converting time-activity data to absorbed doses.
best_for: Turning organ time-activity curves from a PK model into MIRD organ absorbed doses using reference phantoms
notes: Free to download but not open source, and it runs only on Windows with a licensed Microsoft Excel installation.

name: MIRDCalculation
maintainer: MGH Physics Research, Massachusetts General Hospital
description: Voxel-level internal dosimetry applying Lanconelli voxel S-values to SPECT or PET activity maps interpolated onto the CT grid, supporting seven therapeutic radionuclides, with BED, EUD, dose-volume histograms and reports.
best_for: Scripting voxel dosimetry and radiobiological dose metrics for a radioligand cohort inside a Python workflow
notes: MIT licensed, 134 commits. S-value convolution only - no Monte Carlo transport.

name: SlicerOpenDose3D
description: 3D Slicer module for patient-specific molecular radiotherapy dosimetry: image registration and segmentation, time-activity curve fitting across serial SPECT or PET studies, and absorbed dose calculation.
best_for: Going from serial post-therapy images to organ and lesion absorbed doses, end to end and reproducibly
notes: 857 commits with CI, developed since 2019 - the strongest maintenance signal of the dosimetry tools here. Requires a 3D Slicer installation.

name: ADAPT
maintainer: Biomedical Simulations Resource, University of Southern California
description: Computational modelling platform for pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic analysis, developed and supported at USC since 1985.
best_for: Individual and population PK/PD estimation, especially maximum-likelihood and Bayesian individual fitting
notes: Free but not open source - you must submit a Release Agreement. Windows only, and needs Intel oneAPI plus Visual Studio: a real barrier on Mac or Linux.

name: MonolixSuite
description: Monolix for population PK/PD by SAEM, PKanalix for NCA, Simulx for simulation, plus an R API.
best_for: SAEM-based population modelling with a GUI, and NCA plus simulation in one toolchain
notes: Formerly Lixoft; monolix.lixoft.com now redirects here. No pricing or academic terms stated on the page.

name: nlmixr2
maintainer: Matthew Fidler and the nlmixr2 team
description: R package fitting nonlinear mixed-effects models specified as differential equations with flexible dosing, using compiled C from rxode2 to solve the ODEs.
best_for: Learning population PK/PD estimation without paying for a licence
notes: The closest free substitute for NONMEM or Monolix. Needs a C/C++ toolchain (Rtools on Windows). Worked examples include phenobarbital, nimotuzumab and a mavoglurant PBPK model.

name: NONMEM
description: Nonlinear mixed-effects estimation program for population PK and PK/PD, bundled with PREDPP and NM-TRAN. Current version 7.6.
best_for: Fitting population PK/PD models in the format regulators and most industry groups expect
notes: Annual subscription; fee not published. Distributed as Fortran 95 source, so you must supply a compatible compiler. Not usable on a zero budget.

name: Phoenix NLME
description: Nonlinear mixed-effects engine for population PK via a graphical model editor or the Phoenix Modeling Language, with parametric and non-parametric algorithms and VPC output.
best_for: Population PK modelling when you want a GUI rather than a text control stream
notes: Pricing not published. Free Pirana and RsNLME licences are offered for academic use.

name: Pmetrics
maintainer: USC Laboratory of Applied Pharmacokinetics and Bioinformatics
description: R package for non-parametric and parametric population and individual PK/PD modelling and simulation; version 3 runs a bundled Rust engine.
best_for: Non-parametric population PK, where the parameter distribution is not assumed normal
notes: The repo states shareware with a suggested donation rather than a standard open-source licence - read it before institutional use.

name: Pumas
description: Commercial modelling and simulation suite for pharmacometrics built on Julia, sold alongside consulting services.
best_for: Population PK/PD modelling in Julia when speed on large problems matters
notes: Not open source. A Pumas for Academia programme gives complimentary access for non-commercial research; commercial pricing not published. Requires learning Julia.

name: saemix
description: R implementation of the Stochastic Approximation EM algorithm for parameter estimation in nonlinear mixed-effects models fitted to longitudinal data.
best_for: Understanding how SAEM works, or fitting NLME models without a PK-specific dosing layer
notes: Licence not stated on the project page or either GitHub repo - treat as unconfirmed. No NONMEM-style dosing records out of the box.

name: Stan
description: Probabilistic programming platform for Bayesian inference with its own modelling language and interfaces from R, Python, Julia and the shell.
best_for: Learning Bayesian hierarchical modelling before adding PK structure via Torsten
notes: Not pharmacometrics software on its own - dosing, compartments and steady state are things you write yourself, or get from Torsten.

name: Torsten
description: Stan functions for pharmacometric data: one- and two-compartment analytical solutions, matrix-exponential solutions for linear systems, and ODE integration for coupled PK/PD models.
best_for: Fully Bayesian population PK/PD when you want posterior distributions rather than point estimates
notes: The documentation warns it is still a prototype needing further testing before critical use. Uses NONMEM-style data conventions but needs no NONMEM licence. Ships runnable example models. Requires knowing Stan first.

name: PFIM
maintainer: PFIM Group, INSERM / Universite Paris Cite
description: Evaluates and optimises population designs for nonlinear mixed-effects models via the Fisher information matrix: number of groups, subjects per group and sampling times.
best_for: Design evaluation as an independent check on, or alternative to, PopED
notes: PFIM 5.0 (2022) was rewritten around S4 classes, so tutorials written for PFIM 4 and earlier will not run unchanged.

name: PopED
description: Computes optimal experimental designs for population and individual studies based on nonlinear mixed-effects models, generally via Fisher Information Matrix calculations.
best_for: Choosing sampling times and group sizes before a PK study is run
notes: Optimal design assumes you already have a plausible model and parameter values - the answer is only as good as those priors.

name: Alzheimer's Disease Clinical Trial Simulation Tool
description: Drug-disease-trial model for mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's using ADAS-Cog, coupling disease progression, drug effect, dropout, placebo response and sources of variability.
best_for: Learning how a regulator-reviewed model separates progression, placebo and dropout components
notes: NOT directly downloadable: access requires a request form, and the page states the application is under construction. Weak maintenance signal despite the regulatory pedigree.

name: DMD Clinical Trial Simulation Tool
maintainer: Critical Path Institute, Duchenne Regulatory Science Consortium
description: Longitudinal disease-progression models for Duchenne muscular dystrophy covering supine-stand, four-stair climb, ten-metre walk, forced vital capacity and North Star Ambulatory Assessment, with covariates for severity, age, steroid use and mutation.
best_for: A worked multi-endpoint rare-disease progression model usable for trial sizing and enrichment
notes: Genuinely obtainable on application, as a hosted Shiny app or an R package, through the RDCA-DAP portal. EMA has issued a Letter of Support rather than full qualification.

name: Berkeley Madonna
description: General-purpose differential equation solver with a graphical flowchart interface: build models from icons, generate equations, run multiple integration schemes, fit curves.
best_for: Building and seeing an ODE model - including PBPK-style structures - without writing code
notes: Paid; tiers listed but no prices. Used in several published tutorials (the TMDD tutorial supplement among them), which is why it still appears in the literature.

name: Campsis
description: Generic PK/PD simulation platform sitting on top of the rxode2 and mrgsolve engines: create datasets, load models, simulate and plot through one interface.
best_for: Building simulation datasets and scenarios without hand-writing engine-specific code
notes: A wrapper, not an engine - you still need rxode2 or mrgsolve working. Smaller user base than the engines it wraps.

name: CARCADE
description: Agent-based model of CAR T-cell therapy in dish and tissue contexts with healthy cells, cancer cells, cancer stem cells and CD4+/CD8+ CAR T-cell agents, vasculature, and profilers for growth and lysis.
best_for: Spatially resolved questions about CAR T trafficking, exhaustion and CD4/CD8 ratio that compartmental kinetics cannot express
notes: Runs from a jar configured by XML, built on the MASON agent-based library. Nine commits, no releases.

name: CARTmath
description: Shiny simulator of a three-population ODE model of CAR-T therapy in preclinical haematological cancer - tumour cells, effector CAR-T cells and a long-term memory pool - with tumour-induced immunosuppression.
best_for: A first interactive CAR-T model where expansion, contraction and memory persistence can be varied by hand
notes: Run locally via app.R; needs shiny, plotly and DT. Licence not stated. Fourteen commits - a frozen paper companion.

name: mrgsolve
description: R package for simulating hierarchical ODE-based models used in drug development - PK, PK/PD, PBPK and QSP - with a C++ ODEPACK solver and a dosing/event dataset interface.
best_for: Trial simulation and QSP-scale simulation from a model whose parameters you already have
notes: Very active: release 2.0.2, June 2026. Simulation only, no estimation. Ships a built-in model library via mread('pk1', modlib()). Models are written in a C++-flavoured spec, not SBML.

name: PKPDsim
description: R library for numerical integration of ODE systems aimed at PK-PD mixed-effects models, supporting ADVAN-style analytical solutions alongside numerical solving.
best_for: Simulating dosing regimens quickly, including from published literature models
notes: Ships pre-built literature models as installable packages - convenient, but the model is only as good as that transcription.

name: rxode2
maintainer: Matthew Fidler, Wenping Wang, Melissa Hallow
description: R package for simulating from ODE-based pharmacometric models. Equations are written in an R-like mini-syntax, translated to C and compiled.
best_for: Fast simulation from a PK/PD model you wrote yourself; also the solver under nlmixr2
notes: Successor to RxODE - use rxode2 for new work. Needs a C compiler. Simulation only; estimation comes from nlmixr2.

name: serosim
description: Simulates serological survey data from user-specified exposure, immunity and antibody kinetics models, then applies a sampling design to produce observed biomarker data.
best_for: Generating simulated vaccine-response datasets to test an estimation method before applying it to real titres
notes: Companion to serosolver. Four vignette case studies including measles, multi-pathogen and cross-reactive influenza.

name: serosolver
description: Hierarchical MCMC framework fitting a time-since-infection antibody kinetics model - boosting, waning, antigenic seniority - to serological data to reconstruct infection and vaccination histories.
best_for: Estimating antibody boosting and waning parameters from post-vaccination titre data
notes: Installed from GitHub. A stable published branch is maintained for existing projects while the main branch is overhauled.

name: simglucose
description: Python reimplementation of the 2008 UVA/Padova type 1 diabetes glucose-insulin model with 30 in-silico subjects across three age groups, meal scenarios, CGM and pump models, and a Gymnasium environment.
best_for: Running a glucose-insulin PK/PD simulation and testing insulin dosing or closed-loop control without a commercial licence
notes: Explicitly research-use-only: it reimplements an FDA-accepted model but is NOT itself the accepted simulator, which remains commercially licensed. That distinction matters if you cite it.

name: Simulx
description: Clinical trial simulation application: define populations, covariates, parameters and dosing regimens, simulate user-designed scenarios and compute endpoints.
best_for: Trial simulation and what-if dosing scenarios from a model fitted in Monolix
notes: Part of the commercial MonolixSuite; model import is oriented to Monolix/PKanalix projects, so not a general-purpose SBML engine. Has an R API.

name: Thurber Lab ADC model code
maintainer: Greg Thurber lab, University of Michigan
description: Downloadable ADC models: an ADC Designer interface, a Krogh cylinder PBPK model linking tissue and cellular distribution to whole-animal PK, a Krogh cylinder interface, and the SimADC agent-based model.
best_for: Simulating ADC tumour penetration, the binding-site barrier and bystander payload killing rather than plasma PK alone
notes: No licence stated. ADC Designer runs under the free MATLAB Runtime if MATLAB is unavailable; SimADC is a large VirtualBox image.

name: BasiCO
description: Python wrapper exposing COPASI model I/O, time-course simulation, parameter estimation, optimisation, steady-state and sensitivity analysis as plain Python calls.
best_for: Automating COPASI runs from a Jupyter notebook instead of clicking through the GUI
notes: A convenience layer over COPASI, so COPASI's numerics and limitations apply.

name: BioNetGen
description: Rule-based modelling framework using a graph-based language (BNGL) to specify signal transduction, metabolic and gene regulatory networks from structured binding and modification objects.
best_for: Receptor-binding and signalling models where enumerating every complex by hand is impractical
notes: The homepage does not state a licence; the RuleWorld repository does. Requires a Perl runtime, which trips up newcomers - and PySB depends on it.

name: COPASI
description: Simulator and analysis tool for biochemical networks: reads SBML, runs deterministic ODE, SDE and stochastic simulations, and performs parameter estimation and optimisation.
best_for: A first hands-on tool for reaction-network modelling and parameter estimation without writing code
notes: Open source and free for commercial use too. A systems-biology tool, not a PK platform - no built-in dosing regimens, physiology or population machinery.

name: Cytoscape
description: Platform for visualising interaction networks and layering attribute data onto them, extensible through apps, used for molecular and pathway data.
best_for: Exploring and drawing the pathway topology behind a QSP model before any equations are written
notes: Visualisation and network analysis only - it does not simulate dynamics, so it complements rather than replaces a QSP engine.

name: PEtab
description: TSV-plus-SBML format specifying a parameter estimation problem - measurements, observables, noise models, parameter bounds, simulation conditions - outside the model file.
best_for: Making a fitting problem portable and reproducible across estimation tools instead of hard-coding it
notes: A specification, not a solver: you still need a tool that consumes it, such as AMICI or pyPESTO.

name: PySB
maintainer: Lopez Lab (Vanderbilt) and Sorger Lab (Harvard Medical School)
description: Framework for writing rule-based models of biochemical systems as Python programs, using a domain-specific language translated into equations.
best_for: Treating a mechanistic model as version-controlled, testable code rather than a GUI file
notes: Requires Perl and BioNetGen for network generation. A research-group project - support is community-based.

name: sbmlutils
description: Python toolkit built on libsbml for creating and modifying SBML models, adding annotations, converting formats and generating HTML model reports via SBML4Humans.
best_for: Programmatically assembling or annotating SBML models, and producing a readable report of someone else's model
notes: Manipulates models but does not simulate them - pair it with libRoadRunner, COPASI or AMICI.

name: SBtab
description: Table conventions for systems biology data - defined column names plus a syntax for semantic annotations - with an online validator, SBML converter and customiser.
best_for: Keeping model parameters and data in spreadsheets that stay machine-readable
notes: Conventions plus small web utilities, much less widely adopted than SBML. The site names neither maintainers nor a licence.

name: Systems Biology Markup Language (SBML)
description: Open XML-based format for describing computational models in biology, so models can be exchanged and stored independently of the software that built them.
best_for: Understanding why a model built in one tool can be opened in another, and where model repositories get their files
notes: A format, not an application - libSBML and JSBML are the libraries that read and write it. PK concepts such as dosing regimens are largely outside its scope.

name: Virtual Cell (VCell)
maintainer: Center for Cell Analysis and Modeling, UConn Health
description: Platform for modelling cell-biological systems with deterministic, stochastic, spatial and particle-based simulation, from compartmental models to geometry-resolved cellular simulations.
best_for: Spatially resolved sub-cellular mechanism modelling - the one case compartmental QSP tools cannot help with
notes: Free, but simulations run on remote servers backed by a central model database, so the account model is web-based rather than fully local. Licence not stated.

name: httk (High-Throughput Toxicokinetics)
description: Open toxicokinetic data and PBTK models parameterised from in vitro measurements, pre-parameterised for hundreds of chemicals, for IVIVE and reverse dosimetry.
best_for: Running a real PBPK model for a named chemical in one line of R, with parameters already supplied
notes: Built for environmental toxicology, so its physiologies are simpler than PK-Sim or Simcyp. Licence signals conflict - GitHub says MIT, CRAN says GPL-3; check DESCRIPTION before redistributing.

name: PLETHEM
description: Builds and runs PBPK models through a browser-based interface, with master/user/project chemical databases and saveable projects for reproducibility.
best_for: A GUI-driven route into PBPK for toxicology and exposure work without leaving R
notes: Installed from GitHub, not CRAN, and needs an initial local-database setup step. The plethem.com site returned no readable content when checked.

name: Perl-speaks-NONMEM (PsN)
description: Perl programs automating NONMEM model development, from extracting parameter estimates to bootstrap, VPC and stepwise covariate model building. Version 5.7.1, May 2026.
best_for: Running bootstraps, VPCs and covariate model building around NONMEM without scripting each one
notes: PsN is free but drives NONMEM - you still need a paid NONMEM licence for it to be useful. Requires Perl.

name: Pharmpy
description: Pharmacometric modelling package covering dataset and model-file manipulation, automated model-building tools and results reporting. Parses NONMEM models and targets nlmixr2 and rxode2.
best_for: Scripting pharmacometric workflows in Python; the modern successor path to PsN-style automation
notes: Stated as open source but the docs home does not name the licence. NONMEM-backed workflows need a NONMEM licence; the nlmixr2/rxode2 backends do not.

name: Pirana Modeling Workbench
description: Graphical workbench organising pharmacometric workflows across NONMEM, PsN and Xpose/R, tracking model runs and results.
best_for: Keeping track of dozens of NONMEM model runs during model development
notes: Free Pirana licences are available for academic use per Certara's NLME page. Organises other tools - it does not estimate anything itself.

name: bispecific-binding-model
description: Coupled-ODE model of monospecific and bispecific antibody binding to IL-6 and IL-8 receptors, covering binding, transport, internalisation, degradation and ternary complex formation, with data and fitting code.
best_for: Understanding how ternary complex formation and the hook effect arise from binding kinetics
notes: MATLAB for solving and fitting, R for figures. Two commits - a frozen paper companion rather than a maintained tool. Archived at Zenodo.

name: IFN-alpha QSP model (Open Systems Pharmacology)
description: Multiscale QSP model of interferon-alpha-induced JAK/STAT pathway activation in human liver cells, based on Kalra et al. 2019, distributed as a MoBi project with the source publication.
best_for: Seeing a therapeutic protein's receptor-level signalling cascade coupled to PBPK disposition in one model
notes: Requires MoBi, free with the OSP Suite. Eight commits and no named maintainer - a static deposit rather than a developed model.

name: Immune Response Template (IRT)
description: Annotated QSP database of immune-system processes: T, B, dendritic, NK, macrophage and neutrophil populations, over 30 cytokines and immunological synapse molecules, with an oncology version covering the tumour microenvironment.
best_for: Assembling a calibrated immune-response submodel for a biologic instead of hand-coding cytokine networks
notes: Made free of charge in August 2025 but requires registration, and a separate content licence governs reuse - check terms before redistributing. Exports to SBML and SimBiology.

name: ADNI (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative) data
maintainer: ADNI, hosted by LONI at the University of Southern California
description: Longitudinal Alzheimer's cohort data spanning structural, functional and molecular imaging, biofluid biomarkers, cognitive assessments, genetics, omics, neuropathology and remotely collected measures.
best_for: Natural-history longitudinal data for building or validating an Alzheimer's progression or biomarker-trajectory model
notes: Obtainable on application and free: accept the data use agreement and submit an application stating institution and proposed use; review takes about two weeks.

name: Critical Path for Alzheimer's Disease (CPAD) Database
description: Patient-level data from 12,811 patients across 36 Alzheimer's and mild cognitive impairment trials, remapped to CDISC SDTM, holding demographics, APOE4 genotype, medications, MMSE and ADAS-Cog.
best_for: Fitting or replicating an Alzheimer's disease-progression model on real pooled trial data
notes: Available on application to external researchers, no fee stated. Individual trial identities cannot be disclosed under the contribution agreements, so study-level attribution is impossible.

name: FDA DILIrank 2.0 dataset
maintainer: FDA National Center for Toxicological Research
description: Reference list of 1,336 approved drugs ranked by human liver injury risk from labelling and literature: 217 most-concern, 351 less-concern, 414 no-concern and 354 ambiguous.
best_for: A labelled hepatotoxicity ground-truth set for training or benchmarking a prediction model
notes: Free download, no registration. A curated annotation dataset, NOT a mechanistic liver model - it supplies outcome labels, not the mechanism DILIsym provides.

name: NHANES Questionnaires, Datasets and Related Documentation
maintainer: CDC National Center for Health Statistics
description: Downloadable US survey data by component - demographics, dietary, examination, laboratory, questionnaire - for continuous cycles from 1999 to 2025-2026, plus NHANES I-III.
best_for: Building realistic covariate distributions - weight, height, BMI, age, creatinine - for virtual populations in PBPK and popPK simulation
notes: Public download with no login for standard components; the page links a Data User Agreement, and a separate Limited Access category exists for restricted files. Actively updated.

name: nlmixr2data
description: 26 documented example datasets in one R package: theophylline single and multiple dose, warfarin PK/PD, phenobarbital, mavoglurant, nimotuzumab, neonatal weights and 12 simulated ACoP sets.
best_for: The most convenient single source of classic teaching PK/PD datasets in analysis-ready form
notes: Actively maintained. Includes nmtest, a one-compartment dataset with reference NONMEM 7.4.3 output - useful for checking your own solver against a known answer.

name: pharmaverseadam
maintainer: pharmaverse council (GSK, Sanofi, Roche, Novo Nordisk, J&J, Novartis)
description: Synthetic ADaM-format clinical trial datasets generated by running templates from admiral and its therapeutic-area extensions.
best_for: Practising the CDISC data-standards side of pharmacometrics - building analysis datasets in the shape a real submission uses
notes: Actively regenerated when upstream admiral packages release. Sister packages pharmaversesdtm and pharmaverseraw cover the other layers. Data are synthetic, not real patients.

name: Phenobarb (R nlme package)
description: 744 rows from a phenobarbital study in newborn infants given the drug for seizure prevention: subject, birth weight, Apgar score, time, dose and concentration.
best_for: The canonical sparse-sampling population PK teaching dataset, used in nearly every NONMEM course
notes: Cited to Grasela and Donn (1985), with later analyses by Boeckmann, Sheiner and Beal (1994) and Davidian and Giltinan (1995). Stable, no registration.

name: PhysioNet Databases
maintainer: PhysioNet / MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology
description: Hundreds of physiological and clinical databases with software: ECG, EEG, respiratory and wearable-sensor data, imaging, clinical notes and electronic health records.
best_for: Real-world longitudinal patient data - dosing, vitals and labs - for model-informed precision dosing exercises
notes: Three access tiers. Only the Open Access tier meets a download-without-permission bar; Restricted and Credentialed tiers (MIMIC among them) require a data use agreement or formal credentialing.

name: PK-DB
description: Open pharmacokinetics database: 819 studies, 2,454 groups, 17,285 individuals, 2,392 interventions, 138,411 outputs and 6,103 timecourses, curated from published literature.
best_for: Real, curated human PK timecourses and subject-level covariates from published studies via an open API - no registration to read
notes: Figures verified from the live public API endpoint, since the HTML front end is a JavaScript app. Source code released on Zenodo.

name: PKPDdatasets
description: R data package collecting pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic datasets for pharmacometrics and translational medicine, installed from GitHub.
best_for: An extra pool of PK/PD datasets beyond the ones bundled with modelling packages
notes: Verified to exist but thin: 19 commits, datasets not enumerated on the landing page, no licence declared. Treat as a small personal collection, not a maintained repository.

name: PPMI (Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative) data
description: Individual-level longitudinal Parkinson's data spanning clinical assessments, imaging, omics, genetics, digital sensor and biomarker measures, with biospecimen access alongside.
best_for: Longitudinal Parkinson's data for progression modelling or reproducing DAT-imaging enrichment analyses
notes: Obtainable on application, no fee mentioned, review within about a week. Raw genetic data and sequestered assay results need separate approval.

name: Rare Disease Cures Accelerator Data and Analytics Platform (RDCA-DAP)
maintainer: Critical Path Institute, funded by FDA
description: FDA-funded standardised rare-disease data infrastructure covering more than 42 diseases including polycystic kidney disease, Duchenne muscular dystrophy and Friedreich ataxia, supporting progression, biomarker and outcome-measure analysis.
best_for: Pooled patient-level rare-disease natural-history data plus an analysis workspace
notes: Obtainable: platform request, workspace application and a signed data use agreement, free for qualified researchers. 325 approved user requests since the 2021 launch.

name: TB-APEX
description: Curated preclinical tuberculosis data across around 60 studies: in vitro hollow-fibre experiments and in vivo mouse efficacy studies with PK/PD, resistance and microbiology measurements, standardised to CDISC SEND and SDTM.
best_for: Raw hollow-fibre and murine PK/PD data for building translational antitubercular exposure-response models
notes: Obtainable on application and free. The rare case where the underlying hollow-fibre experimental data, not just the method, can actually be had.

name: TB-PACTS
maintainer: Critical Path Institute with WHO/TDR and TB Alliance
description: Patient-level tuberculosis trial data including REMoxTB, RIFAQUIN and OFLOTUB across 39 listed studies, normalised to a TB-specific CDISC standard so studies can be pooled, with susceptibility, adverse events and outcomes.
best_for: Pooled TB trial data for time-to-culture-conversion or treatment-outcome modelling
notes: Obtainable on application and free: platform account, data access request and steering committee approval, up to four weeks. Working knowledge of CDISC SDTM is effectively a prerequisite.

name: Theoph and Indometh (R datasets package)
description: Theoph: 132 rows from 12 subjects with weight, dose, time and concentration, from an oral theophylline study, 11 samples over 25 hours. Indometh sits alongside it.
best_for: The authoritative, citable home of the two classic teaching PK datasets - already installed with any R
notes: Theoph's cited primary source is Boeckmann, Sheiner and Beal (1994), NONMEM Users Guide Part V. Permanently stable, no registration.

name: A platform IgG PBPK model in tumor bearing mouse
description: SimBiology implementation of a platform IgG PBPK model for a mouse bearing a HER2-overexpressing tumour, built on Shah and Betts 2012, with adjustable antigen level, binding parameters and physiology.
best_for: The closest public implementation of the Shah and Betts platform mAb PBPK model, extended with a target-bearing tumour
notes: Last updated 2019. Licence bundled but terms not shown on the page. Needs MATLAB plus the commercial SimBiology toolbox, and a MathWorks account to download.

name: BioModels
description: 3,595 mathematical models of biological and biomedical systems in standard formats: 1,096 manually curated, 1,666 non-curated, 833 auto-generated. Literature-based and freely downloadable.
best_for: Downloading a curated, runnable SBML model of a signalling or disease pathway
notes: The page announces a transition to the University of Florida with a new URL at biomodels.org, which returned 403 when checked - the EBI URL remains the working entry point. Licence terms vary by model.

name: bioPBPK
description: PBPK models for biologics: a Julia implementation of the Jones 2019 monoclonal antibody PBPK model, and an mrgsolve implementation adapted to bamlanivimab.
best_for: Reading a runnable whole-body mAb PBPK model in two languages rather than reconstructing one from a paper appendix
notes: Small repository, 10 commits, no licence file. mAb only - no ADC or bispecific models despite the name.

name: DDMoRe Model Repository
description: Free repository of pharmacometric models - 128 models as of March 2018, of which 51 encoded in PharmML alongside the original NONMEM and Monolix control streams.
best_for: Published population PK/PD control streams; still the largest free collection of NONMEM-style pharmacometric models
notes: EFFECTIVELY DORMANT. Models are still downloadable but every date signal stops in 2018, and the page flags an unresolved bug where new registrations did not receive login credentials. Use as a static archive.

name: depot: a collection of models for mrgsolve
description: R package of 13 published models with vignettes, several for biologics: secukinumab PK/PD, an Fc-osteoprotegerin fusion, and epoetin alfa and filgrastim target-mediated disposition models.
best_for: A worked TMDD parameterisation for a therapeutic protein that runs immediately in R
notes: Installed from GitHub with subdir='pkg'. No explicit licence shown. Requires mrgsolve.

name: Exemplary Protein PBPK Models
description: A PK-Sim project file holding two large-molecule PBPK models - the CDA1 antibody (Taylor 2008) and a domain antibody (Sepp 2015) - built on PK-Sim's protein physiology.
best_for: Seeing how two-pore and lymph-flow physiology is parameterised for an antibody versus a small domain antibody
notes: Repository archived October 2025 and read-only. Requires PK-Sim 7.1 or later. Distinct from the main OSP model library, which is small-molecule.

name: JWS Online
description: Browser-based tool for construction, modification and simulation of kinetic models plus storage of curated models, running time evolutions, steady states and metabolic control analysis.
best_for: Simulating a curated kinetic model in a browser with no install
notes: Model count could not be verified - the model listing is blocked to automated fetching. The most recent publication cited is 2004 and the page has no recent-activity timestamps, so currency is uncertain.

name: Open Systems Pharmacology GitHub organisation
description: Around 400 public repositories behind PK-Sim and MoBi: the PBPK model library, qualification reports, OSPSuite-R, the SimModel calculation engine and workflow packages.
best_for: The umbrella entry point - free PBPK software plus every model, report and R interface that goes with it
notes: Active through mid-2026. Licences differ per repository and are not stated at organisation level.

name: OSP PBPK Model Library
description: Library of released whole-body PBPK substance models with evaluation reports - around 45 compounds including midazolam, rifampicin, itraconazole, digoxin and sildenafil.
best_for: Getting a published, qualified PBPK model for a real drug and re-running or extending it, without asking anyone
notes: Actively maintained, with open issues and pull requests at time of check. Licence not stated on the repo page.

name: OSP Qualification Reports
description: Qualification packages regenerated with each OSP release: DDI reports for CYP1A2, CYP2C19, CYP3A4, P-gp and UGT; paediatric ontogeny packages; and a chronic kidney disease report.
best_for: Seeing how a PBPK platform is formally qualified against clinical data - complete worked examples
notes: Clearly alive: latest release July 2026. Licence not stated on the repo page.

name: PBPK model of antibody brain uptake
description: Reduced brain PBPK model of a non-targeting monoclonal antibody after intravenous and intracerebroventricular dosing, supplied as both an SBML file and a SimBiology project.
best_for: Modelling antibody CNS exposure and comparing systemic against direct intracerebroventricular administration
notes: Companion code to Van De Vyver et al. 2022. Four commits, no licence file. The SBML export means it can be run without SimBiology.

name: Physiome Repository
description: Curated collection of CellML and FieldML models plus musculoskeletal scaffolds, browsable by category with a curation status assigned by the CellML repository curators.
best_for: Physiological and cell-level models in CellML, with curation flags indicating which actually simulate
notes: Site loads and search works, but the welcome page carries no last-updated or model-count signal, so activity could not be confirmed. Same resource as the CellML model repository.

name: BioNumbers
maintainer: Milo lab, Weizmann Institute of Science
description: Searchable database of molecular and cell biology reference numbers with literature citations for each value.
best_for: Finding a cited value for a cell count, protein concentration, turnover rate or volume when parameterising a QSP model
notes: Search interface is live, but total entry count and licence terms are not stated on either the search or About page.

name: EPA Physiological Information Database (PID)
description: Physiological parameter values for PBPK modelling - alveolar ventilation, blood flows, tissue volumes, glomerular filtration rate - for humans across all life stages and for laboratory rodents.
best_for: Sourcing defensible, literature-traced system parameters when building a PBPK model rather than copying a textbook table
notes: STATIC ARCHIVE: final release September 2009, page last updated 2010. Still freely downloadable and still the most complete free compilation of its kind.

name: The Human Protein Atlas
description: Nine data sections - Tissue, Brain, Single Cell, Subcellular, Cancer, Blood, Cell Line, Structure and Interaction - plus focused sets for the secretome, membrane proteome and druggable proteome.
best_for: Establishing target, enzyme and transporter expression across human tissues when specifying compartments in a QSP or PBPK model
notes: Actively updated into 2026. Described as open access, but the specific licence is not stated on the landing page - check before redistribution.

name: adc_cui: post-marketing assessment of antibody-drug conjugates
description: Scripts and data comparing trastuzumab emtansine and trastuzumab deruxtecan: population PK, uncertainty simulation, exposure-response, model-based meta-analysis and a clinical utility index, with a Shiny app.
best_for: A worked ADC exposure-response and benefit-risk pipeline on real approved products
notes: No licence file. Some scripts call lixoftConnectors, so full reproduction needs commercial Monolix; the utility-index and plotting steps are pure R.

name: BioSimulations
description: Portal for publishing, discovering and running dynamical biology simulation projects packaged as COMBINE/OMEX archives, supporting 60+ algorithms across 20+ simulation tools.
best_for: Rerunning a published simulation exactly as the authors specified it - model, experiment and expected output in one archive
notes: Genuinely runnable in-browser, but small: the public API listed only around 10 projects, mostly textbook models. Documentation activity spans 2019-2021, so maintenance may have slowed.

name: cptpsp-tutorial-2019 (QSP and PBPK with mrgsolve)
description: Complete code for the CPT:PSP hands-on tutorial: a voriconazole PBPK model, an extended version with mechanistic oral absorption and intestinal clearance, and a MAPK QSP model.
best_for: The best single worked example of a published PBPK plus QSP tutorial you can clone and rerun end to end
notes: Includes model files, digitised clinical observations, a virtual population and tissue composition data. A snapshot tied to the 2019 paper rather than an evolving project; no explicit licence file.

name: Metrum Research Group GitHub organisation
description: Around 120 public repositories spanning pharmacometrics and QSP: mrgsolve, Torsten, pkgr, bbr, pmplots and mrgda, plus tutorial repositories accompanying published papers.
best_for: Browsing an entire open pharmacometrics toolchain plus the paper-accompanying model code
notes: Highly active through mid-2026. Licences differ per repository - mrgsolve GPL-2, Torsten BSD-3-Clause.

name: PumasAI Labs GitHub organisation
description: Around 25 repositories of workshop and tutorial material: Bayesian, optimal design, ACoP and PAGANZ NLME workshops, and DeepPumas workshop code.
best_for: Downloading complete conference-workshop code and slides for population NLME, Bayesian and optimal-design modelling
notes: Active into 2026. The code targets Pumas, whose full product is commercial, but the workshop repositories themselves are public.

name: Reproducibility Study on a PBPK Model of FcRn-Mediated Recycling for Large Molecules
description: Curated, executable reproduction of de Witte et al. 2023: a whole-body PBPK model with explicit FcRn binding in plasma and endosomes for IgG and FcRn inhibitors, shipped as an OMEX archive.
best_for: A verified, citable FcRn recycling model whose published figures have been independently regenerated
notes: Runs in MoBi v11, free with the OSP Suite. CC BY 4.0, so compatible with this site's licence. Reproducibility-certified - unusually strong provenance for a biologics model.

name: TCE: T cell engager simulation code
description: Two-scale simulation of bispecific T cell engagement: a kinetic Monte Carlo model of engager, CD3 and tumour-antigen three-body binding, and a Langevin dynamics model of T cell redirection to tumour cells.
best_for: Interrogating how affinity and antigen density shape trimer formation, below the resolution of ODE models
notes: Fortran source with no build system or licence file, though the README explicitly permits free sharing and reuse. Requires a Fortran compiler.

name: ChEBI - Chemical Entities of Biological Interest
description: Manually curated database and ontology of chemical entities - over 195,000 entries covering natural and synthetic small molecules used to intervene in living systems.
best_for: Getting an ontology-grounded chemical identity and classification for a compound used in a model or dataset
notes: Described as open access but no specific licence is stated, so recorded as unknown.

name: ChemSpider
description: Free chemical structure database giving access to over 100 million structures aggregated and deduplicated from hundreds of sources, with links back to the originating sources.
best_for: Resolving a name, synonym or structure to identifiers and comparing physicochemical values across sources
notes: Free to search, but neither the homepage nor the About page states any data licence or terms of use - redistribution rights unverified.

name: DrugBank
description: Commercial drug knowledgebase of drug profiles, targets, pathways, chemical structures, diseases, clinical trials and companies, searchable online with a free account.
best_for: A quick consolidated drug monograph - targets, metabolism, ADME notes - when you accept you cannot redistribute what you read
notes: THE BIGGEST LICENCE HAZARD HERE. The site states use or redistribution of any DrugBank content requires a licence. Academic dataset downloads were suspended at time of check. Only a small Open Data subset is CC0. Do not redistribute.

name: DrugCentral
