maintainer: Division of Translational Informatics, University of New Mexico
description: Online drug compendium: around 4,995 active ingredients and 152,476 pharmaceutical products with bioactivities and indications, plus veterinary coverage.
best_for: Linking an approved drug to its targets, indications and regulatory identifiers in one openly licensed download
notes: CC BY-SA 4.0, so compatible with this curriculum's licence. Share-alike applies to derivatives; no academic/commercial split stated.

name: PubChem
licence: mostly public domain; depositor content varies
maintainer: NCBI, US National Library of Medicine
description: NCBI's chemistry database - the largest free chemistry database - holding depositor-contributed substances, standardised compounds and bioassay results.
best_for: Getting a structure, identifier or physicochemical property for a compound in seconds
notes: NCBI states no restrictions on its molecular databases but warns PubChem also contains depositor material protected by copyright, and that NCBI cannot grant unrestricted redistribution. Check per-record provenance.

name: Clinical Trials Information System (CTIS) public portal
maintainer: EU/EEA national competent authorities and ethics committees
description: Public portal of the EU Clinical Trials Information System, covering individual trials launched since 31 January 2022 across up to 30 EU/EEA countries.
best_for: Checking the current authorised protocol and status of an EU trial started under the Clinical Trials Regulation
notes: Trials started before 31 January 2022 are in the older EU Clinical Trials Register instead. No data-reuse or download statement on the page.

name: ClinicalTrials.gov
licence: public domain by convention; not stated on site
description: Registry and results database of clinical studies; the API reports around 600,000 study records, each retrievable as structured JSON including design, arms, eligibility and posted results.
best_for: Finding dose levels, sampling schedules and populations actually studied for a compound before building a trial-simulation scenario
notes: Record count verified from the public API, which needs no key; the web UI is JavaScript-rendered. No explicit licence statement was retrievable.

name: EU Clinical Trials Register
maintainer: European Medicines Agency and Heads of Medicines Agencies
description: Legacy EU register displaying information on EudraCT trials; the page states all ongoing EU/EEA trials are now shown through CTIS instead.
best_for: Retrieving protocol and result-summary details for older EudraCT-era European trials
notes: Now essentially a historical archive alongside CTIS. No record counts or reuse terms given.

name: WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform
description: Platform aggregating records from a network of primary trial registries, including ClinicalTrials.gov, into one search portal; WHO coordinates the network rather than running a registry.
best_for: Catching trials registered outside the US and EU registries when scoping global evidence for a compound
notes: Access via the trialsearch portal, an API, monthly downloads and a records folder on request. No reuse licence stated on this page.

name: C-Path Disease Modeling Coalition, paediatric IBD programme
maintainer: Critical Path Institute with ESPGHAN and the Crohn's and Colitis Foundation
description: Initiative announced October 2025 to build regulatory-grade quantitative disease-progression models, beginning with paediatric Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis as proof of concept.
best_for: Tracking whether a regulatory-grade paediatric IBD progression model becomes available, and who holds the data
notes: NOTHING IS AVAILABLE YET. A launch announcement and an open call for data contributors, listed here as the clearest example of a consortium that is not yet a resource.

name: Critical Path Institute Quantitative Medicine Program
description: C-Path's model-informed drug development programme, listing its regulatory-endorsed outputs: Alzheimer's trial simulation tools, an early-motor Parkinson's tool, a Duchenne progression model, and the PKD total kidney volume biomarker.
best_for: Seeing which disease-progression models have actually reached FDA endorsement or EMA qualification
notes: An index of what exists, not a source. The page asserts models are open-source platforms, but every tool sits behind a separate request form.

name: Polycystic Kidney Disease Outcomes Consortium (PKDOC)
maintainer: Critical Path Institute with the PKD Foundation, FDA, EMA and Health Canada
description: Consortium that qualified total kidney volume as a prognostic enrichment biomarker for ADPKD trials; FDA additionally designated it a reasonably likely surrogate for disease progression under accelerated approval.
best_for: A concrete case study of a biomarker taken through dual FDA and EMA qualification
notes: The qualification decision is freely readable. The underlying database of around 2,674 subjects is open to non-members subject to data use committee approval.

name: DailyMed
licence: public domain (site); label text from manufacturers
description: The most recent labelling submitted to FDA and currently in use: over 157,000 labelled submissions covering prescription and OTC human and animal drugs, devices and supplements.
best_for: Reading the current Structured Product Label, including the clinical pharmacology and DDI sections, for a marketed US product
notes: Offers bulk download of all labels plus web-service APIs. Label content originates from manufacturers even though the site itself is public domain.

name: Drugs@FDA
description: Searchable record of FDA-approved drug products by name, active ingredient or application number, with current approved labelling and FDA staff review documents.
best_for: Retrieving the clinical pharmacology review or approval package behind a dosing decision - the single best free source of worked regulatory analyses
notes: Excludes CBER-regulated products such as vaccines and cell therapies - use the Purple Book for those.

name: electronic medicines compendium (eMC)
description: UK regulated medicines information: Summaries of Product Characteristics and patient leaflets for licensed medicines, browsable by product name or active ingredient.
best_for: Reading the UK SmPC, pharmacokinetic properties section included, for a licensed medicine
notes: Free to browse but run by a commercial company. The legal and privacy notice returned 404 when checked, so do not assume redistribution rights for SmPC text.

name: EMA Medicines database
description: Database of centrally authorised human and veterinary medicines and herbal products, with European Public Assessment Reports and product information.
best_for: Locating the EPAR and its clinical pharmacology and popPK sections for an EU-centrally-authorised medicine
notes: Nationally authorised medicines are not covered. Offers Excel download of medicine data. No reuse licence could be verified - EMA's legal notice pages returned 404 when checked.

name: FDA Orange Book
description: FDA-approved drug products with therapeutic equivalence evaluations, searchable by name, ingredient, application number, dosage form and route, plus patent and exclusivity data.
best_for: Checking therapeutic-equivalence coding and patent status when framing a generic bioequivalence question
notes: Downloadable data files updated monthly.

name: FDA Purple Book
description: All FDA-licensed biological products including biosimilars, interchangeable products and their reference products, plus CBER-regulated products, searchable by brand or generic name.
best_for: Establishing which biologic is the reference product and whether a biosimilar is rated interchangeable
notes: Includes a data export. Complements Drugs@FDA, which excludes CBER products.

name: openFDA Drug Labeling API
description: API serving FDA Structured Product Label files for prescription and OTC drugs, annotated and converted to JSON; records span June 2009 onward.
best_for: Programmatically mining label sections - CYP interaction or renal-impairment text - across hundreds of products at once
notes: Terms state most content is CC0: copy, modify, distribute even commercially without asking permission. Third-party data with restricted rights is marked. Call volume may be limited.

name: bioRxiv
description: Preprint server for biology, letting scientists share findings before peer review and formal publication.
best_for: Catching new pharmacology and modelling methods months before journal publication
notes: Each preprint carries the licence its authors selected, so redistribution rights must be checked per item.

name: Europe PMC
maintainer: EMBL-EBI with the Europe PMC Funders' Group
description: Life-sciences literature search over articles, preprints and more, free to anyone, with RESTful APIs, an OAI service and bulk downloads for developers.
best_for: Full-text searching rather than abstract-only, across articles and preprints including grant-linked literature
notes: Reuse rights depend on each record's own licence - open-access subsets differ from abstract-only records.

name: medRxiv
description: Preprint repository for the health sciences, hosting preprints across more than 50 subject categories.
best_for: Finding pre-publication clinical evidence - dosing, trial results, pharmacogenomics - for a drug under active study
notes: No screening or licensing terms on the landing page; per-preprint licences apply.

name: PubMed
licence: public domain for citation records; full text varies
description: More than 40 million citations for biomedical literature from MEDLINE, life science journals and online books, with links to full text at PubMed Central and publisher sites.
best_for: Systematically finding the primary PK/PD literature behind a model assumption - and the tool this curriculum verifies every citation against
notes: Free to search. Full-text articles including PMC content are protected by copyright - abstracts and full text are not automatically redistributable.

name: Semantic Scholar
licence: unknown; API governed by a licence agreement
description: Free research tool for scientific literature indexing over 237 million papers across all fields, with citation context and an API offering paper search.
best_for: Tracing citation networks across pharmacometrics and machine-learning literature at once
notes: Free to use with no paywall. The API and datasets are governed by a separate licence agreement whose terms were not on the fetched page.

name: Critical Path Institute Tools and Platforms index
description: Directory of six clinical trial simulation and enrichment tools and eleven disease databases spanning Alzheimer's, Duchenne, Parkinson's, multiple sclerosis, polycystic kidney disease, rare disease and tuberculosis.
best_for: The single entry point for locating a C-Path disease-specific tool or database and its access route
notes: A directory, not a download page. Tools are web applications and databases are portals; each requires separate registration and, for most, committee approval.

name: Pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic models for time courses of antibiotic effects
maintainer: Minichmayr, Aranzana-Climent and Friberg, Uppsala University
description: Searchable catalogue of published antibiotic PK/PD time-kill models indexed by drug and pathogen, recording bacterial growth structure, effect equation, regrowth and resistance handling, interactions and PK parameters.
best_for: Finding a prior structural model and starting parameters for a specific antibiotic-pathogen pair
notes: Free web tables with the underlying data on GitHub. Content last updated September 2021, so newer agents are missing.

name: Tumour growth inhibition (TGI) model library documentation
description: Documented catalogue of TGI structures: unsaturated growth (linear, quadratic, exponential, Simeoni, Koch) and saturated (logistic, Gompertz, Von Bertalanffy), with log-kill against Norton-Simon killing and Claret or two-population resistance.
best_for: Choosing and writing down the right tumour growth, kill and resistance equations before fitting anything
notes: The DOCUMENTATION is free to read without a licence and carries the full ODE systems and analytical solutions - that is the value. The executable library ships with commercial MonolixSuite.

name: KEGG: Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes
description: Integrated database collection spanning PATHWAY, BRITE, MODULE, ORTHOLOGY, GENES, GENOME, COMPOUND, REACTION, ENZYME, NETWORK, DISEASE, DRUG and MEDICUS.
best_for: Getting a curated pathway or drug-metabolism map to scaffold a QSP or systems model
notes: LICENCE TRAP. The legal page states KEGG is not a public database and is not publicly funded. Academic users may browse free for research; academic service providers need a subscription; commercial users must license through Pathway Solutions. Do not redistribute.

name: Reactome Pathway Database
maintainer: EMBL-EBI, NYU Langone, OHSU and OICR
description: Free, open-source, curated and peer-reviewed pathway database. Version 97, June 2026: 2,883 human pathways, 16,423 reactions, 11,694 proteins, 2,188 small molecules and 43,308 literature references.
best_for: Sourcing a reaction-level, literature-referenced pathway topology to seed or sanity-check a mechanistic model
notes: Data under CC0 with no attribution required and commercial use permitted; illustrations CC BY 4.0; software Apache 2.0. Very much alive, with quarterly-style releases.

name: The Gene Ontology Resource
description: Computational representation of gene function across molecular, cellular and tissue-system levels: GO terms plus annotations linking gene products to those terms across many species.
best_for: Assigning consistent functional vocabulary to targets or gene sets in a mechanistic or omics-linked analysis
notes: CC BY 4.0. Redistribution should name the Gene Ontology, the release date and the Zenodo DOI, and keep the copyright notice and warranty disclaimer.

name: WikiPathways
maintainer: Community-curated; Maastricht University and Gladstone Institutes
description: Open science platform of biological pathways contributed, updated and used by the research community, with pathways available as GPML, GMT and SVG and through APIs.
best_for: Grabbing an editable, freely redistributable pathway diagram when KEGG's licence blocks reuse
notes: CC0 public-domain dedication - the safest pathway source for a curriculum that must redistribute content.

name: CPIC - Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium
description: Peer-reviewed gene-drug prescribing guidelines; the CPIC API returns 29 guideline records including CYP2D6 and opioids, CYP2C9/VKORC1 and warfarin, and TPMT/NUDT15 and thiopurines.
best_for: Deciding whether a genotype should change the dose of a specific drug, and by how much
notes: cpicpgx.org now redirects to clinpgx.org, which is JavaScript-only, so no licence text could be read. Guideline inventory verified through the open API. Do not redistribute guideline content without checking.

name: FDA Table of Pharmacogenetic Associations
description: FDA-evaluated drug-gene pairs in three sections: associations supporting therapeutic management recommendations; those affecting safety or response; and those with potential impact on pharmacokinetics only.
best_for: Seeing which pharmacogenetic associations FDA itself considers PK-relevant versus dosing-actionable
notes: Page content last updated October 2022 - check the current label too. FDA stresses inclusion does not mean testing must precede prescribing.

name: FDA Table of Substrates, Inhibitors and Inducers
description: FDA tables of in vitro CYP marker reactions, selective inhibitors and inducers, clinical index substrates, inhibitors and inducers, and transporter substrates and inhibitors.
best_for: Choosing a regulatorily acceptable index substrate, inhibitor or inducer when designing or simulating a DDI study
notes: Content current as of June 2023. Explicitly not exhaustive; entries selected on sensitivity, specificity and safety, drawing on the University of Washington Drug Interaction Database.

name: Predictive Safety Testing Consortium (PSTC)
maintainer: Critical Path Institute with FDA, EMA and PMDA
description: Safety-biomarker qualification consortium whose qualified outputs include a six-biomarker composite urinary kidney panel, seven rodent kidney biomarkers, and glutamate dehydrogenase for liver injury.
best_for: Finding qualified kidney and liver safety biomarkers and their formal contexts of use
notes: Documents yes, models no. The user's guide, FDA qualification letters and summary data packages download free; no quantitative DILI or AKI model is distributed.

name: BindingDB
licence: CC BY 3.0; CC BY-SA 3.0 for ChEMBL-derived rows
description: Public database of measured binding affinities: around 3.2M measurements across 1.4M compounds and 11,500 protein targets, of which 1.6M curated entries cover 772,000 compounds and 4,800 targets.
best_for: Assembling a target-affinity dataset with the measurement technique attached - the thing P-04 says an IC50 is meaningless without
notes: Two licences coexist: BindingDB-curated content is CC BY 3.0, while rows ingested from ChEMBL carry CC BY-SA 3.0, and that share-alike obligation follows them.

name: ChEMBL
description: Manually curated database of bioactive molecules with drug-like properties, combining chemical, bioactivity and genomic data across compounds, assays, activities, targets and source documents.
best_for: Pulling literature-extracted potency data for a compound series, or the assay context behind a reported IC50
notes: CC BY-SA 3.0 - share-alike follows any redistributed derivative, which matters if you build a teaching dataset from it.

name: IUPHAR/BPS Guide to PHARMACOLOGY
maintainer: IUPHAR and the British Pharmacological Society
description: Expert-curated guide to pharmacological targets with quantitative ligand data across eight target classes: GPCRs, ion channels, nuclear receptors, kinases, catalytic receptors, transporters, enzymes and others.
best_for: Finding a curated, referenced affinity value and the recommended target nomenclature for a drug-target pair
notes: CC BY-SA 4.0, so compatible with this curriculum's own licence - one of the few sources here that is. Commercial users are directed to a sustainability statement on access fees. The site now requires registration to browse.

name: Open Targets Platform
description: Integrates public genetics, genomics, drug and literature datasets to support systematic identification and prioritisation of drug targets, linking targets, diseases and drugs.
best_for: Checking the genetic and tractability evidence linking a target to a disease before committing to a QSP model
notes: Data dedicated to the public domain under CC0 with no downstream restrictions; code Apache 2.0. All contributing sources agreed to unrestricted use. One of the cleanest licences in this table.

name: UniProt
description: Protein sequence and functional annotation knowledgebase; the reference source for canonical protein identity, isoforms, sequence features and cross-references.
best_for: Pinning down the exact protein isoform, sequence and accession behind a named drug target or transporter
notes: CC BY 4.0 applies to copyrightable parts of the databases - BY-SA compatible. Main site is JavaScript-only; the licence text is at rest.uniprot.org/help/license.

name: ACoP - American Conference on Pharmacometrics
description: ISoP's annual conference, with tutorials, Special Interest Group events, a hackathon and student programming.
best_for: The main US-facing pharmacometrics meeting; worth tracking even if you only watch recorded sessions later
notes: Paid registration. Recorded ACoP sessions later appear on learn.isop.org, some free. Note go-acop.org still serves 2023 content.

name: ASCPT Annual Meeting
maintainer: American Society for Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics
description: In-person annual meeting covering the discovery, development, regulation and utilization continuum.
best_for: Clinical pharmacology breadth rather than pure modelling depth
notes: Paid registration; rates not published on this page. ASCPT also publishes CPT:PSP, the journal most of this curriculum's tutorial references come from.

name: PAGE - Population Approach Group Europe
description: Annual European meeting for data analysis using the population approach. The site hosts an archive of every abstract ever submitted, searchable by year back to 1992.
best_for: The abstract archive is free and is a genuinely useful literature source in its own right
notes: Archive is browsable without login at no cost - the highest-value piece for an unfunded learner. Attending requires paid registration and travel.

name: QSPC - Quantitative Systems Pharmacology Conference
maintainer: Leiden University and the Foundation for the Advancement of Systems Pharmacology
description: Conference on emerging computational and experimental approaches in QSP and PBPK/PD, with plenary lectures and posters.
best_for: People specifically working in QSP who want the European community meeting
notes: Paid registration, fees not shown. Held roughly every four years in the Netherlands, so not an annual fixture.

name: Advanced Master in Pharmacometrics (UCLouvain and KU Leuven)
description: One-year, 60-ECTS advanced master taught in English in Brussels Woluwe, run jointly by UCLouvain and KU Leuven.
best_for: Graduates who want a dedicated one-year pharmacometrics degree in Europe
notes: Requires on-site enrolment in Belgium; fees not stated on the programme page.

name: Buffalo MS in Pharmacometrics and Personalized Pharmacotherapy (Online)
maintainer: University at Buffalo School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
description: 30-credit MS completable fully online in about two years, part-time option available, covering mathematical models for disease and drug measurement, PK, PD and systems pharmacology.
best_for: Someone already working who wants an accredited US master's without relocating
notes: Requires admission and paid tuition; rates not stated on the page. No public course material.

name: Florida Model-Informed Drug Development graduate certificate
maintainer: University of Florida College of Pharmacy
description: 12-credit online certificate over three semesters: Introduction to Quantitative Pharmacology plus three of Intro to MIDD, Physiologically Based Modeling, Population PK/PD, and QSP Modeling.
best_for: Formal PBPK/QSP/PopPK coursework from the UF pharmacometrics group without a full degree
notes: Paid enrolment; tuition not stated. Some Fall sections are on-campus only. Credits transfer into the UF online MS.

name: Florida MS in Pharmaceutical Sciences, MIDD specialization
maintainer: University of Florida College of Pharmacy
description: 32-credit fully online MS specialising in MIDD: population PK/PD, QSP and PBPK modelling, with electives in pharmacoeconomics and precision medicine. Most finish in 2-3 years.
best_for: Career-changers who need a US graduate degree in pharmacometrics at a distance
notes: Requires admission and paid tuition. Non-degree single-course enrolment is offered as a lower-commitment entry point.

name: Manchester MSc Model-based Drug Development
description: 12 months full-time in person or 29 months part-time by distance learning, covering PK, PD, pharmacometrics, systems pharmacology and PBPK.
best_for: A UK MSc with a genuine part-time distance-learning route
notes: Fees stated on the page: full-time GBP 20,000/yr UK and GBP 37,800/yr international; part-time distance GBP 10,000/yr UK. Needs a 2:2 honours degree and IELTS 7.0.

name: UCSF PhD in Pharmaceutical Sciences and Pharmacogenomics
description: PhD programme whose core sequence covers pharmacokinetic principles, metabolism and transport and applied PK, with an advanced PK/PD course offered biennially.
best_for: Prospective PhD applicants wanting PK/PD inside a pharmacogenomics curriculum
notes: Doctoral admission required. The courses page lists descriptions and instructors only - no syllabi or slides are downloadable.

name: Uppsala MSc in Pharmaceutical Modelling
description: Two-year, 120-credit master's taught in English covering mechanistic and AI/ML modelling, PK, computational chemistry and bioinformatics, ending in a 30-credit thesis.
best_for: EU/EEA/Swiss students, for whom this is a tuition-free route into a top pharmacometrics group
notes: No tuition for EU/EEA/Swiss citizens; others pay SEK 330,000 total. Requires full-time on-site enrolment in Sweden.

name: ISoP Learning Center
description: ISoP's education platform: the MIDD webinar series, on-demand webinars, recorded ACoP sessions, and Special Interest Group programmes including the QSP Virtual Student Symposium.
best_for: Keeping current with what practising pharmacometricians are arguing about
notes: Mixed access. MIDD webinar items are USD 50 for non-members, free for members; several SIG items are free to non-members with a free guest account. Note isop.org is a different organisation (pharmacovigilance).

name: Metrum Open Courseware
description: Fifteen full courses released openly: R for Pharmacometrics, Essentials of Population PK-PD, Advanced Topics, Bayesian modelling, Stan/Torsten, mrgsolve, and PBPK/QSP in R.
best_for: The highest-value free resource here - a complete self-study pharmacometrics curriculum, no login, no cost
notes: Free with no registration, materials under CC BY 3.0. Some courses date from 2010-2018 but the population PK-PD and Bayesian content is still standard.

name: MIT OpenCourseWare HST.151 Principles of Pharmacology
description: Graduate pharmacology course archive with lecture notes, problem sets and solutions, and exams with solutions, covering drug mechanisms, distribution and metabolism.
best_for: Filling in the biological pharmacology foundation that pure modelling courses assume you already have
notes: Free, no registration, fully downloadable, CC BY-NC-SA. Spring 2005 materials - dated on specific agents but sound on principles.

name: Principles of Clinical Pharmacology
maintainer: NIH Office of Clinical Research Education and Collaboration Outreach
description: Free asynchronous course: 7 modules, 48 recorded core lectures plus case studies on pharmacokinetics, drug metabolism and transport, special populations and pharmacogenomics.
best_for: The single best free structured grounding in clinical pharmacology before touching modelling software
notes: No institutional affiliation needed. Formal registration runs in yearly cycles, but the lectures are publicly viewable any time via the NIH PCP YouTube playlist and NIH VideoCast.

name: Applied Pharmacometrics Training (APT) Fellowship
maintainer: Pharmacometrics Africa NPC with CP+ Associates
description: 24-week virtual fellowship plus two week-long face-to-face sessions; fellows work on model-based analysis projects with industry, consultancy and academic partners.
best_for: Early-to-mid-career African PhD holders who need funded, mentored project experience rather than lectures
notes: Fully funded including airfare, accommodation and a stipend. Eligibility is narrow - PhD, African residency, prior clinical pharmacology project experience. Applications run in cycles.

name: Buffalo Pharmacometrics Modeling micro-credential
maintainer: University at Buffalo School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
description: Asynchronous online three-course series - Biometry, Intermediate PK, Population PKPD Modeling - with software training and a final modelling assessment, typically three semesters.
best_for: A working scientist who wants a credential smaller than a full MS but still credit-bearing
notes: Paid per-credit tuition. Requires a science bachelor's and prior pharmacometrics background verified by the programme director.

name: Certara Academic Teaching License Program
description: Grants no-cost Phoenix, RsNLME and Pirana licences to degree-granting institutions for classroom teaching, plus free webinars, tutorials, videos and software guides.
best_for: Instructors and their enrolled students who need commercial PK software for coursework at no cost
notes: Requires institutional affiliation: licences go to institutions for teaching, not research, and need a Certification of Use signed by a Dean or legal representative.

name: Certara University
description: Over 25 on-demand and live courses in PK fundamentals, Phoenix WinNonlin, NLME, IVIVC and PML coding, plus certifications in NCA and population modelling.
best_for: Practitioners who need a recognised Phoenix or NCA credential and can pay for it
notes: Paid, most courses USD 90-575. Around 50% academic discount and 25-75% reduction for Africa and India residents.

name: Introduction to Pharmacokinetics: From ADME to PK/PD
description: Covers how a drug is dosed, absorbed, distributed, metabolised and eliminated, how PK properties are predicted from compound testing, and how PK and ADME are monitored in early development.
best_for: A gentle first pass at PK concepts for someone with no pharmacology background
notes: Audit track gives video access; verified track adds readings and assessments. Price was not displayed - confirm audit availability at enrolment.

name: Introduction to Small Molecule Drug Discovery and Development
maintainer: University of Cape Town, on Coursera
description: Four-module course; module 3 covers in vitro ADME, DMPK, PK/PD modelling and human dose prediction, alongside disease biology, medicinal chemistry and trial phases.
best_for: Understanding where pharmacometrics sits in the wider drug development pipeline
notes: Free audit access to the material; a paid certificate is needed for graded assignments. Coursera account required, no institutional affiliation.

name: Starting with the OSP Suite
description: Introductory course on Open Systems Pharmacology fundamentals: PBPK and QSP principles, PK-Sim, MoBi, the R toolbox, absorption routes, special populations and regulatory context.
best_for: Anyone starting PBPK who wants a guided path through PK-Sim/MoBi rather than raw documentation
notes: Free registration for academics. Pricing for non-academic users is not shown. Requires an account.

name: UPSS - Uppsala Pharmacometric Summer School
description: Two-week residential summer school for PhD students worldwide, capped at 30 participants; each attendee submits an abstract and presents a poster.
best_for: PhD students with some NONMEM experience who want intensive hands-on training at no course fee
notes: No course fee, but accommodation and travel are not covered; limited travel grants exist. Requires PhD student status and prior NONMEM experience.

name: EUFEPS - European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
description: Federation of around 15,000 pharmaceutical scientists across industry, academia, government and regulators, running eight topic networks plus conference series.
best_for: European students wanting regulatory-science and pharmaceutical-sciences context
notes: Membership fees not stated. Networks are broad pharmaceutical sciences rather than pharmacometrics-specific. Runs a European PhD Student Competition.

name: ISoP Discussion Forum
description: Active pharmacometrics discussion forum run by ISoP, with categories for PopPK and PKPD, systems pharmacology, clinical pharmacometrics, and tool-specific threads on NONMEM, R and Monolix.
best_for: Asking a question a tutorial does not answer - the field's main public question-and-answer venue
notes: Free to browse. Whether reading requires registration was not stated on the page. This is why The Modeler's Bench does not run its own forum: the community already exists here.

name: PAGANZ - Population Approach Group in Australia and New Zealand
description: Southern-hemisphere pharmacometrics society meeting annually since 1999, pairing hands-on workshops taught by senior figures with a scientific conference.
best_for: Anyone in Australia or New Zealand; the workshops are the main draw
notes: Membership itself is free and confers voting rights. Meeting registration fees are not stated on the site.

name: RedIF - Red Iberoamericana de Farmacometria
description: Ibero-American pharmacometrics network founded 2017, running workshops, congresses and webinars in Spanish and Portuguese, plus multicentre studies and training.
best_for: Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking learners for whom English-only material is the real barrier
notes: Membership via an external platform with member discounts on congress registration; prices not shown.

name: ARLO - Access to Regulatory Learning Opportunities
description: Searchable index of training resources - courses, webinars, videos, workshops, guidelines and papers - contributed by EMA, FDA, WHO, USP and SAHPRA among others.
best_for: Finding free training on a specific regulatory or modelling topic without knowing who published it
notes: Free to browse and search with no registration; anyone can submit a resource.

name: nlmixr2 vignettes and worked examples
description: Getting-started articles, a cheat sheet and worked example models: phenobarbital with correlations, nonlinear PK/PD (nimotuzumab), PBPK (mavoglurant) and PKPD myelosuppression.
best_for: Someone with R but no NONMEM licence who wants to fit nonlinear mixed-effects models tonight
notes: Free and open source, no registration. Vignettes are readable without installing anything.

name: Pharmacometrics Africa Online Learning Portal
description: Moodle site hosting around 18 open-access quantitative clinical pharmacology courses, including a self-paced 12-lesson pharmacometrics course in English and French.
best_for: A self-learner with no institution who wants a structured course tonight
notes: Free self-registration for the self-paced course; some courses are restricted to enrolled delegates. Site is migrating to learn.pmxafrica.org.

name: Pumas Tutorials
description: Seven structured learning paths: Julia fundamentals, Pumas fundamentals, model development, simulation, covariate and censored-data workflows, bioequivalence, Bayesian and TMDD.
best_for: Learning modern pharmacometric workflow end to end from worked examples, even if you never run Pumas
notes: Free to read online with no login. The Pumas software itself is separately licensed - reading the tutorials costs nothing.
